description-block.comment: @Description holds free-form prose, not C++. Handing that prose to the embedded source.cpp grammar is what causes scope leaks that silently break highlighting for the rest of the file: an apostrophe in ordinary prose ("the material's behaviour") opens string.quoted.single.cpp, a stray double quote opens string.quoted.double.cpp, and a sentence shaped like 'A B, C (D)' opens meta.declaration.cpp - none of which ever close, because prose has no matching delimiter and ends sentences with '.' not ';'. The keyword injection cannot rescue the string cases, since its selector deliberately excludes -string. So the block is consumed here instead, with no 'include' of source.cpp: everything between @Description and the closing brace is inert text, scoped as string.unquoted.description.mfront so themes render the prose the way they render a string literal. The begin pattern deliberately does not require '{' on the same line, because '@Description' followed by '{' on the next line is common in real files. The end pattern does NOT simply match the next '}': real descriptions embed LaTeX, and those braces are not balanced ('\left\{ ... \right.' opens one that is never closed), so neither a plain '\}' nor a brace-counting rule terminates in the right place. What is reliable in practice is that the block's own closing brace sits alone on its line, hence '^\s*\}\s*;?'; '\}\s*;\s*$' additionally covers the single-line form '@Description{ ... };'. The last alternative, '^(?=\s*@[A-Za-z]\w*)', is a safety net: an '@Description' with no block yet - what the file looks like while the user is still typing - degrades to plain highlighting instead of swallowing every directive below it. This rule must be included BEFORE '#keywords', otherwise '#keywords' matches '@Description' first and the body falls through to source.cpp.
description-block.name: meta.description.mfront

bounds-interval.comment: @Bounds / @PhysicalBounds intervals use an inverted bracket to mark an open (infinite) endpoint, e.g. '@PhysicalBounds M in [0:*[;' (see the MFront book). That leaves an unmatched '[' on the line. Without this single-line 'match' rule the '[' falls through to the embedded source.cpp grammar, which treats it as the start of the multi-line meta.bracket.square.array.cpp begin/end pair. That pair never finds its ']' and stays open for the rest of the file, so every '@Xxx' keyword after the first bounds declaration silently loses keyword.control.mfront. IMPORTANT: in the root 'patterns' list this rule is included BEFORE '#keywords': both start at the same index on a '@Bounds' line, and TextMate resolves that tie by list order.

keywords.name: keyword.control.mfront
keywords.comment: Full list of MFront '@Xxx' keywords, including the interface-specific ones (@Abaqus*, @Aster*, @Castem*, @Cyrano*, @UMAT*, @CalculiX*, @Ansys*) and the generic-behaviour ones (@Gradient, @Flux, @ThermodynamicForce, @TangentOperatorBlock(s)). Alternatives are ordered longest-first: TextMate alternation is leftmost-first, not longest-match, so '@TangentOperator' listed before '@TangentOperatorBlocks' would match only the shorter prefix and leave 'Blocks' unhighlighted. Regenerate with `mfront --help-keywords-list` rather than by hand.
